title: Garment workers protest in Gazipur over minimum wage

tea.why: Workers are protesting against a proposed 36% minimum wage increase, which they argue is insufficient to cover rising living costs.
tea.want: A minimum monthly salary of Tk 25,000, along with regular bonuses, social security benefits, and improved working conditions.
tea.changed: Nov 26: Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse workers attempting to block a highway in Gazipur.

summary: Garment workers in Gazipur, Bangladesh, have engaged in multi-day protests to demand a higher minimum wage. The unrest intensified following a government-appointed panel's decision to approve a 36% wage increase, which workers and labour advocates rejected as inadequate. Protesters have blocked major highways and engaged in clashes with law enforcement, with reports of a police motorcycle being set on fire. Police have responded by deploying tear gas and sound grenades to disperse crowds and restore order. While factory owners have expressed concerns that higher wages could threaten the industry's financial viability, workers maintain that the proposed Tk 17,000 monthly salary fails to meet basic household needs. The industrial area remains tense as authorities continue to monitor the situation, with factories facing ongoing disruptions to production.
response: Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse protesters, according to the Gazipur Industrial Police. The government-appointed wage board approved a 36% increase, which employers argue is the maximum sustainable amount.

updates.text: Workers protested in Gazipur against a proposed Tk 17,000 minimum wage, leading to clashes with police.
Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse workers attempting to block a highway following a 36% wage increase announcement.
